description.narrative: One in 14 Egyptian children has never attended school (UNICEF 2010). This includes children from poor, urban households living in informal settlements in Cairo, which often lack public services and infrastructure such as schools and health centres. A Population Council survey (2011) concluded that levels of absenteeism, repetition and dropouts demonstrate the internal efficiency of the education system is low. Data from UNHCR indicates that at least 50% of young refugees from countries such as Sudan, Somalia, Ethiopia, Eritrea and Iraq are not attending formal schooling. In addition to bureaucratic and language barriers, many refugee children do not access public education in Egypt due to experiences of racism and xenophobia. Refugee Youth Project will work with Children’s Cooperative to facilitate a young person-led research project exploring refugee and Egyptian children’s experiences of education in Cairo. This project will engage young refugees and Egyptians in gathering information from peers, community members, teachers and professionals to improve understanding of the barriers that some children face in accessing and/or achieving in education, to propose potential solutions to the challenges, and to inform advocacy efforts on educational rights for all children. It will build mutual understanding and shared goals amongst young refugees and Egyptians.
